verdict.tagline: Massive scale and heavy demands make survival an uphill battle.
for_you_if: you have high-end hardware to handle optimization issues
you are prepared for heavy demands on your storage space
you enjoy deep survival crafting despite performance friction
not_for_you_if: you are short on storage space
you need stable frame rates on release hardware
you want polished gameplay without frequent crashes

I enjoyed playing this game. 
But by god how I am glad that I am in the refund window; this game is one massive archive file surrounded by smaller ones. That means that if you don't have 200gb+ free storage above downloading the game (totaling 400gb) you cannot update the game without reinstalling.

citations.review_text: awsome game once you get into it....but updates are too frequent

I would like to recommend this, but after seeing all the stupid changes that happened from ASE to ASA, im seriously dissapointed

The game is incredibly buggy, it lags to high hell even on low settings, and genuinely the allied AI in this game is so stupid that they get in my way when I'm trying to fight for my life to survive or it just straight up steals the food directly out of your food box. My complaints: Some really poor texture bugs seem to just litter the landscape (sideways rock overlays, weird movement of plants), and it is diabolical to place DLC only animals in the world that cannot be tamed unless you pay for them. Also, the character creation is still janky af, but less so by a smidgen.

My Pros: love the mini-map addition, Evo had a very  hard map to follow. I also enjoy the amount of texture detail you can add or subtract to the graphics in settings, very helpful. 

This is essentially the same game as ARK Survival Evolved but with better graphics and differences of UI. I was expecting more, but perhaps in later installments we will get more. Get this game on sale and only on sale is my take. Enjoy it for what it is worth (about $12-$19 lol).

claims.claim: Reviewers state that official servers are heavily impacted by cheaters, aimbotters, and exploiters.

citations.review_text:
Such a shame what an absolute disappointment this money-grab-game has been. I played so much ASE as well, and Ark is one of my favorite games ever. It had so much potential to be amazing, but the devs are either incapable or unwilling to make a healthy game. Cheating has always been a huge problem but is at an all time high right now, and nothing is done about it. There are more cheaters on official than non-cheaters, and it's not even close. Every tribe runs a gacha bot, aimbotters and ESP on every server and at every fob, and meshing has never been easier. But what's even more insane is that it's easier to fight the cheaters than the insanely overpowered p2w creatures added into the game intentionally. I've wanted to give the benefit of the doubt that things will improve for so long, but it's painfully obvious that Wildcard and Snailgames are happily running this franchise into the ground in an effort to squeeze a bit more money out of their fans.

Do youself a favor and skip this one.

I've loved ARK for years. I've put countless hours into this game and made some amazing memories playing PvP with friends. But at this point, it's getting harder and harder to justify playing it, let alone recommending it to anyone else.

The game is completely broken when it comes to PvP. Cheaters, dupers, and meshers run rampant, and Wildcard seems to do next to nothing about it. You can spend weeks or even months building up your base, grinding resources, and raising dinos, only to lose everything to someone exploiting the game.

And when that happens? **You're on your own.** Wildcard won't roll back a server after you've been meshed to hell, they won't restore your lost items or dinos, and they won't compensate you for anything. Meanwhile, the people blatantly violating Wildcard's own Code of Conduct continue getting away with it.

What's even more frustrating is that **more and more content is being locked behind paywalls**, while the core game and its PvP experience remain riddled with exploits. You're expected to keep spending money on a game where legitimate players aren't protected and cheaters face little to no consequences.

I genuinely love ARK, and that's what makes this so disappointing. This game has so much potential, but the way it's being handled is driving away the very players who have supported it for years.

**I cannot recommend that anyone spend their hard-earned money on this game right now, and honestly, probably ever at this rate.** Unless you're planning to play PvE or privately with some friends, save yourself the money, time, and frustration.

**The biggest threat in ARK PvP isn't the enemy tribes. It's the cheaters Wildcard allows to ruin the game.**

claims.claim: Reviewers describe frequent, massive game updates that require hundreds of gigabytes of free storage space just to install.

citations.review_text: I have played this game as PvE with my family. I also played ARK: Survival Evolved previously with them. I did not pay for the premium game content or the new maps or dinosaurs. The taming and breeding of dinos is still relatively fun with a few new ones thrown in. I don't normally write any reviews, but I was particularly dissatisfied with my experience in this game. Firstly, the developers don't seem to care about issues you may have if you don't own a premium gaming computer. On my older gaming computer, the graphics really aren't that much better than the previous version of the game. They actually hindered play a lot of the time. citations.review_text: It's impossible to tolerate this game anymore. Want to play single player? TOO BAD! Increasingly longer loading times between sessions for no reason and countless bugs make that nothing more than a fantasy. How about multiplayer? HOW ABOUT NO!? Yeah, Snail Games seems to hate PVPers, because every "fantastic tame" basically says "**** YOU" to those people, and Wildcard can't be bothered to actually fix any PVP exploits, instead applying a band aid to those issues and calling it a day. I used to adore this game, I really did. But whatever game I loved then is no longer here, replaced by whatever sorry excuse for a game this is. I wanted to like this game, but even Wildcard can't seem to care for it, so why should you? If you're on the fence on buying this game, hop off it this instant and stay far away from it. This is not the game you loved. This is not the Wildcard you knew in 2015. Both of those things died the moment this abomination released. Good day to you, and good riddance to this buggy, unoptimized, downright unplayable mess Snail Games has the audacity to make us pay for.

This game is basically unplayable.  After 1000 hours attempted in ASA...I think I'm finally done with it.  Maybe someone will make a good dino tame game that is actually good...this isn't it!

claims.claim: Reviewers report severe performance drops and frame rate issues when opening the in-game inventory.

citations.review_text: I love this game and was really exited about the Tides expansion. After the last few updates I go from 100+fps to 8-9 fps when i open up my inventory. It is pretty much unplayable

To start, I would love to play this game everyday, however, the current operating state of the game is ridiculous! There are issues this game has had for years that disrupt being able to enjoy the game. I have a couple thousand hours on the PS4 version of Survival Evolved, about 1,600 plus hours on PC Survival Evolved, and a hundred plus hours on Survival Ascended. I will not return to playing this game, or purchasing any additional content until major bug fixes are completed. For example, the issue with the screen changing to split screen after looking at your inventory, and not being able to get your view back to normal. That should be a priority fix! Not TLC-ing more dinos. Then there is the issue with every update being like a new full install that takes forever! So unnecessary! I Will not give this Wild Card studio or Snail any more of my hard earned money until I see proof that this studio cares about the functionality of it's product. Perhaps if that happens I may change my rating and review.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that cheaters and exploiters run rampant on official PvP servers while developers fail to address the issue.

citations.review_text:
Such a shame what an absolute disappointment this money-grab-game has been. I played so much ASE as well, and Ark is one of my favorite games ever. It had so much potential to be amazing, but the devs are either incapable or unwilling to make a healthy game. Cheating has always been a huge problem but is at an all time high right now, and nothing is done about it. There are more cheaters on official than non-cheaters, and it's not even close. Every tribe runs a gacha bot, aimbotters and ESP on every server and at every fob, and meshing has never been easier. But what's even more insane is that it's easier to fight the cheaters than the insanely overpowered p2w creatures added into the game intentionally. I've wanted to give the benefit of the doubt that things will improve for so long, but it's painfully obvious that Wildcard and Snailgames are happily running this franchise into the ground in an effort to squeeze a bit more money out of their fans.

Do youself a favor and skip this one.

I've loved ARK for years. I've put countless hours into this game and made some amazing memories playing PvP with friends. But at this point, it's getting harder and harder to justify playing it, let alone recommending it to anyone else.

The game is completely broken when it comes to PvP. Cheaters, dupers, and meshers run rampant, and Wildcard seems to do next to nothing about it. You can spend weeks or even months building up your base, grinding resources, and raising dinos, only to lose everything to someone exploiting the game.

And when that happens? **You're on your own.** Wildcard won't roll back a server after you've been meshed to hell, they won't restore your lost items or dinos, and they won't compensate you for anything. Meanwhile, the people blatantly violating Wildcard's own Code of Conduct continue getting away with it.

What's even more frustrating is that **more and more content is being locked behind paywalls**, while the core game and its PvP experience remain riddled with exploits. You're expected to keep spending money on a game where legitimate players aren't protected and cheaters face little to no consequences.

I genuinely love ARK, and that's what makes this so disappointing. This game has so much potential, but the way it's being handled is driving away the very players who have supported it for years.

**I cannot recommend that anyone spend their hard-earned money on this game right now, and honestly, probably ever at this rate.** Unless you're planning to play PvE or privately with some friends, save yourself the money, time, and frustration.

**The biggest threat in ARK PvP isn't the enemy tribes. It's the cheaters Wildcard allows to ruin the game.**
